ticket.title: miter lookup and other CLI reads fail while the miter mcp server holds the redb index
ticket.description: DID NOT REPRODUCE on 2026-10-30, macOS 12.7.6, and the reason is now measured rather than guessed: three miter mcp daemons were live (PIDs 27438/36335/46165, one per VS Code extension host, one window per workspace), but lsof shows NONE of them holds <suite>/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb or any .gaugeblock path - they serve other workspaces. So this index was unheld: miter lookup StorypoleStore exited 0 with correct coordinates, and miter index . performed a full 877-file write (5571 symbols) and exited 0. Daemon RSS 2-3 MB each, so not a memory cost either. The original report may have been real against an older redb or a CLI that opened the index exclusively, but it needs a reproduction. The failure that IS measurable is index staleness - filed as GB-237.

verification_receipt.summary: Closed as superseded: the symptom did not reproduce with three miter mcp daemons live and none holding the suite redb file. The real defect is index staleness, tracked as GB-237.

task.title: miter lookup and other CLI reads fail while the miter mcp server holds the redb index
task.description: The mcp server has been running for two days and holds miter.redb exclusively, so miter lookup --context fails with the database is held by another process while miter impact succeeds with a shared lock. Any agent that has the MCP server registered loses the CLI read path entirely, which is the path the harness tells agents to use for context slicing. Either the MCP server should hold a shared lock while idle, or reads should fall back to a read-only open, or the CLI should name the owning process.
